brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A handmade green tea from Tianyin village in Duping town, Zhenyuan County, Guizhou.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Local tradition places its fame as early as the Tang and credits Wu Sangui and Ortai with raising its reputation in the Ming and Qing; a folk song recalls Wu Sangui trading tea for horses here. It was shown twice in Beijing in the 1960s. Its revival is dated to 2002, and a six-part standard system for it passed expert review in December 2012, with over ten thousand mu of gardens in the area.
processing: Mainly made by hand in the traditional way.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Shapely and emerald, likened to a sword tip or a tender lotus bud.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: A long aftertaste, holding up over many infusions.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
